title: i recreated a childhood game with Fable experiments
author: Low-Cook-3544
selftext: i used to play piano tiles where you press them to the beat and thought to match it with GTA styles now that the hype is on. Not sure how to make it a full good game tbh but it was a really fun experiment and i'm mindblown by the assets - going to take this as a template to an ai game maker

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body:
Tbh very simple. I literally went into claude and used this prompt for Fable high (pasted below), then I ported the game into Rosebud so that i can host it on an ai gamedev platform for players + keep editing. They usually add in the latest models a few weeks after they're launched but their current collection is already really good:

Build a single self-contained, instantly playable HTML browser game (Three.js via CDN): a music rhythm game where you make a fully procedural cartoon lowrider dance in time with the beat. Generate a looping upbeat synth/funk track entirely in code via the Web Audio API (no external files) with a clear steady beat. The car is built from primitives — glossy body, chrome rims, hydraulics on each corner. Controls: A = front hop, D = back hop, W = full bounce, S = lean/sway. Score is based on how close each input lands to the beat (Perfect/Good/Miss popups), with a combo meter, animated beat-timing bar at the bottom, exhaust smoke + sparks on good hits, and a sunset boulevard backdrop with palm trees. Auto-plays a little idle bounce so it looks alive before input. Turn-on-your-audio energy, fun in 10 seconds, no instructions needed, screen-recordable.
